Windowed timeOpt sedimentation rate estimation

Source: R/win_timeOpt.R
win_timeOpt.Rd

The win_timeOpt function conducts a windowed timeOpt sedimentation rate estimation. This function is based on timeOpt and eTimeOpt of the 'astrochron' package, but allows for multithreaded analysis, windows of fixed duration, a correction of the r-squared values for their bias towards high sedimentation rates, a mask of rates that cannot be tested and an obliquity version of the fit.

Usage

win_timeOpt(
  data = NULL,
  window_size = 10,
  sedmin = 0.5,
  sedmax = 2,
  numsed = 100,
  limit = FALSE,
  fit = 2,
  fitModPwr = TRUE,
  flow = NULL,
  fhigh = NULL,
  roll = 10^6,
  targetE = c(405.7, 130.7, 123.8, 98.9, 94.9),
  targetP = c(20.9, 19.9, 17.1, 17.2),
  targetO = c(53.6, 41, 39.6),
  targetOmod = 173,
  detrend = TRUE,
  normalize = TRUE,
  linLog = 1,
  window_mode = c("depth", "time"),
  window_duration = 1500,
  step = 1,
  centres = NULL,
  bias_correction = c("null", "none"),
  noise_model = c("auto", "ar1", "powerlaw"),
  n_null = 50,
  null_rho_step = 0.05,
  null_beta_step = 0.1,
  null_smooth = 2,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_samples = 3,
  min_cycles = 2,
  null_cache = NULL,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  normalise = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Record to analyse (matrix or data frame with two columns: depth in metres in column 1, proxy value in column 2), evenly sampled (the depth steps must be equal within 0.1 percent; use e.g. linterp of 'astrochron' to resample). Must be given (the NULL default fails). Default=NULL.

window_size

Thickness of the moving window in metres (numeric, > 0), only used with window_mode = "depth". Default=10.

sedmin

Lowest sedimentation rate of the grid (numeric, > 0, in cm/kyr). Default=0.5.

sedmax

Highest sedimentation rate of the grid (numeric, > sedmin, in cm/kyr). Default=2.

numsed

Number of sedimentation rates of the grid between sedmin and sedmax (integer, >= 1; 1 tests sedmin only). Default=100.

limit

Limit the evaluated sedimentation rates to the range in which the full target signal can be recovered (logical, TRUE or FALSE; passed to timeOpt). Only used with window_mode = "depth"; the untestable mask (min_samples, min_cycles) is usually the better choice. Default=FALSE.

fit

Which amplitude modulation is tested (numeric, one of 1, 2, 3): 1 precession modulated by eccentricity, 2 short eccentricity modulated by the 405-kyr cycle, 3 obliquity modulated by the obliquity modulation periods (targetO, targetOmod; see Details). Default=2.

fitModPwr

Include the modulation periods in the spectral power fit (logical, TRUE or FALSE; passed to timeOpt; not used for fit = 3). Default=TRUE.

flow

Low-frequency cut-off of the Taner bandpass filter that isolates the carrier (numeric, half power point in cycles/kyr). NULL uses the default of timeOpt for fit = 1 and fit = 2, and 1/46 for fit = 3. Default=NULL.

fhigh

High-frequency cut-off of the Taner bandpass filter (numeric, half power point in cycles/kyr). NULL uses the default of timeOpt for fit = 1 and fit = 2, and 1/36 for fit = 3. Default=NULL.

roll

Roll-off rate of the Taner filter (numeric, > 0, in dB/octave); larger values give steeper filter edges. Default=10^6.

targetE

Eccentricity periods to evaluate (numeric vector, in kyr), in order of decreasing period with 405 kyr (or 405.7) first. Default=c(405.7, 130.7, 123.8, 98.9, 94.9).

targetP

Precession periods to evaluate (numeric vector, in kyr), in order of decreasing period; used for fit = 1 and in the spectral fit. Default=c(20.9, 19.9, 17.1, 17.2).

targetO

Obliquity carrier periods (numeric vector, in kyr), only used for fit = 3. Default=c(53.6, 41.0, 39.6).

targetOmod

Obliquity modulation periods (numeric vector, in kyr) used in the envelope fit of fit = 3. Default=173.

detrend

Remove a linear trend from every window before the analysis (logical, TRUE or FALSE); also used for the noise model fit. Default=TRUE.

normalize

Divide the raw r-squared curve of every window by its maximum, so that it peaks at 1 (logical, TRUE or FALSE). The bias-corrected z-scores are not normalised. Default=TRUE.

linLog

Spacing of the sedimentation rate grid (numeric, 0 or 1): 0 linear, 1 logarithmic. Default=1.

window_mode

How the window is defined (character, one of "depth", "time"): "depth" a window of fixed thickness window_size (the behaviour of earlier versions); "time" a window of fixed duration window_duration for every trial sedimentation rate, which removes most of the bias towards high rates (see Details). Default="depth".

window_duration

Duration of the window in kyr (numeric, > 0), only used with window_mode = "time"; its thickness at a trial rate is window_duration * sedrate / 100 m. Default=1500.

step

Spacing of the window centres in samples: every step-th data point is a window centre (integer, >= 1); larger values are faster. Ignored when centres is given. Default=1.

centres

Depths of the window centres to evaluate (numeric vector, in metres; each is moved to the nearest sample); overrides step. NULL uses step. Default=NULL.

bias_correction

Correction of the r-squared values for their bias towards high sedimentation rates (character, one of "null", "none"): "null" standardises them against noise series of a fitted noise model and gives z-scores and family-wise probabilities (see Details); "none" only returns the raw r-squared values (much faster). Default="null".

noise_model

Noise model of the correction (character, one of "auto", "ar1", "powerlaw"): "ar1" AR(1) red noise, "powerlaw" \(f^{-\beta}\) noise, "auto" the one of the two that fits the periodogram of the window best (Whittle likelihood). Only used with bias_correction = "null". Default="auto".

n_null

Number of noise series per grid node of the noise model (integer, >= 1); more series give more stable z-scores and probabilities and take longer (the family-wise probabilities need at least 5). Default=50.

null_rho_step

Step of the grid of AR(1) coefficients on which the noise level is computed and interpolated (numeric, between 0 and 1); smaller steps are more precise and slower. Default=0.05.

null_beta_step

Step of the grid of power-law exponents on which the noise level is computed and interpolated (numeric, > 0). Default=0.1.

null_smooth

Half width (in grid steps of the sedimentation rate, integer >= 0) of the moving average of the noise mean and standard deviation over neighbouring rates; 0 means no smoothing. Default=2.

alpha

False-alarm level of the family-wise threshold z_threshold and of the column significant (numeric, between 0 and 1). Default=0.05.

min_samples

Minimum number of samples per shortest carrier cycle (precession for fit 1, short eccentricity for fit 2, obliquity for fit 3) for a rate to be testable (numeric, > 0; in tests timeOpt still worked with 3.4 samples per shortest precession cycle). Default=3.

min_cycles

Minimum number of cycles of the longest fitted period that the window must span for a rate to be testable (numeric, > 0). Default=2.

null_cache

Noise tables to reuse: the null_cache element of an earlier result of win_timeOpt with the same settings (list); missing grid nodes are added. NULL computes all tables. Default=NULL.

run_multicore

Run the windows and the noise simulations in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used when run_multicore = TRUE (integer; NULL: an automatic, safe number: physical cores minus one, at most 4, and limited by the free memory). Set options(waverider.n_cores = ...) to change the default. A value > 1 also switches on parallel computing. Results do not depend on the number of cores. Default=NULL.

verbose

Show progress bars of the window and noise computations (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

normalise

British spelling of normalize; if given (not NULL) it overrides normalize. Default=NULL.

Value

Returns a list of class win_timeOpt.result with the elements

r_2_envelope, r_2_power, r_2_opt

matrices (sedimentation rate x window) of the raw r-squared values (normalised when normalize = TRUE)

r_2_envelope_avg, r_2_power_avg, r_2_opt_avg

their averages over all windows

sedrate

the sedimentation rates (cm/ka)

x, y

depth and proxy value of the window centres

linLog

the linLog value

z_envelope, z_power, z_opt

z-scores against noise (NULL when bias_correction = "none"; NA for untestable cells)

z_envelope_avg, z_power_avg, z_opt_avg

their averages over all windows

p_fw

family-wise probability that noise reaches z_opt anywhere on the rate grid

z_threshold

family-wise 1 - alpha threshold of z_opt per window

best_sedrate, best_z, p_best, significant

per window: the rate with the highest z_opt among the testable rates (raw r2_opt when there is no correction), its z-score and family-wise probability, and whether p_best < alpha

untestable_code, testable

see Details

noise_family, noise_param

fitted noise model per cell (1 = AR(1) coefficient, 2 = power-law exponent)

npts

number of points of each window

data

the input data

window_mode, window_size, window_duration, fit, bias_correction, noise_model, alpha

the settings

null_cache

the noise tables, for reuse

Details

Bias towards high sedimentation rates. In a window of fixed thickness, a higher trial sedimentation rate means a shorter time span, so fewer cycles of the target periods fit in the window. The envelope fit and the spectral power fit then have fewer independent data points per fitted sinusoid, and for red noise the target frequencies move to the strong low-frequency end of the spectrum. Both raise the r-squared values that pure noise reaches, so the raw r-squared surface has a rising baseline, and a genuine peak at a low sedimentation rate can be smaller than the noise level at high sedimentation rates.

Windows of fixed duration (window_mode = "time"). For every trial sedimentation rate the window is cut to window_duration kyr (its thickness is window_duration * sedrate / 100 m), so every rate is tested on the same number of cycles. This removes most of the bias at its source. Rates whose window does not fit in the record around a given depth are marked as untestable there. timeOpt is run once per rate. With window_mode = "depth" (default) the window has a fixed thickness window_size (the behaviour of earlier versions).

Noise-level correction (bias_correction = "null"). For each window a noise model is fitted to the periodogram (Whittle likelihood; for time windows on the window of the middle rate that fits in the record): an AR(1) spectrum (flat at low frequencies, bending to f^-2) and a power law (f^-beta, e.g. pink noise for beta = 1). With noise_model = "auto" the better-fitting one is used. Noise series of the same model, length and sample spacing are analysed with exactly the same timeOpt settings. This gives, for every trial sedimentation rate, the mean and standard deviation of the noise r-squared values (on a logit scale, because r-squared is bounded by 0 and 1). These are smoothed over neighbouring rates (null_smooth) and the observed values are expressed as z-scores: $$z_{env} = (logit(r^2_{env}) - \mu_{env}) / \sigma_{env}$$ and likewise for the spectral power fit; both are combined (Stouffer's method) as \(z_{opt} = (z_{env} + z_{pwr}) / \sqrt{2}\). A z-score of 0 is the noise level at that sedimentation rate. To keep the computation affordable, the noise level is computed on a grid of model parameters (steps null_rho_step and null_beta_step; for depth windows also three window lengths) and interpolated. The noise tables can be reused with null_cache.

Probabilities. For each grid node the maximum z_opt over all testable rates is recorded for every noise series. This gives a family-wise false-alarm threshold per window (z_threshold, the 1 - alpha quantile) and a family-wise probability per cell (p_fw): the probability that noise reaches this z-score anywhere on the rate grid.

Untestable rates (untestable_code): 1 = fewer than min_samples samples per shortest carrier cycle (precession for fit 1, short eccentricity for fit 2, obliquity for fit 3); 2 = the window spans fewer than min_cycles of the longest fitted period; 3 = the window does not fit in the record. Untestable cells get no z-score.

Obliquity version (fit = 3): timeOpt fit 1 with obliquity carrier periods (targetO) bandpassed between flow and fhigh (default 1/46-1/36 cycles/kyr) and the obliquity modulation periods (targetOmod) in the envelope fit. A precession record read as obliquity gives a peak at half the true rate, an obliquity record read as precession (fit 1) a peak at twice the true rate; compare the fits with win_timeOpt_multi.

References

Meyers, S.R. (2019). Cyclostratigraphy and the problem of astrochronologic testing. Earth-Science Reviews 190, 190-223 <doi:10.1016/j.earscirev.2018.11.015>

Author

Based on the timeOpt and eTimeOpt functions of the 'astrochron' R package.

Examples

# \donttest{
#Conduct a windowed timeOpt on the magnetic susceptibility record
#of the Sullivan core of Pas et al., (2018).
set.seed(1)
mag_win_timeOpt <- win_timeOpt(
data = mag[1:250, ],
window_size = 6,
sedmin = 0.1,
sedmax = 1,
numsed = 5,
limit = FALSE,
fit = 2,
fitModPwr = TRUE,
flow = NULL,
fhigh = NULL,
roll = 10 ^ 6,
targetE = c(405.7, 130.7, 123.8, 98.9, 94.9),
targetP = c(20.9, 19.9, 17.1, 17.2),
detrend = TRUE,
normalize = TRUE,
linLog = 1,
bias_correction = "null",
n_null = 6,
noise_model = "ar1",
step = 10,
run_multicore = FALSE,
verbose = FALSE)
# }
